newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians mass for new protest on Tirana square.
newsitem.headline: Albanians mass for new protest on Tirana square.

text.p: Up to 30,000 people gathered on the Albanian capital Tirana's main square on Sunday to protest at losing their life savings in pyramid investment schemes and calling on the government of President Sali Berisha to resign.

Eyewitnesses said the crowd, which had earlier gathered in a nearby soccer stadium, was being led by several opposition leaders, in apparent defiance of government warnings last week against mass demonstrations.
Earlier, some 1,000 to 2,000 protesters had run straight into a wall of riot police as they made their way from the stadium to the central Skanderbeg Square.
"People hurled stones pushing back riot police as they tried to head towards the Martyrs of the Nation boulevard (leading off the main square), an eyewitness told Reuters.
Addressing the crowd in the stadium, opposition leaders accused Berisha's right-wing Democratic Party and the government of exploiting the investment schemes for their own gain.

Violent protests against the collapse of the schemes have spread across the small Balkan nation. Demonstrators have smashed buildings and set town halls on fire in a number of citys in Europe's poorest country.
